# Middleware, sessions, cookies, security (verified on soli 2.28.2; not rechecked on 2.36.3)

## Middleware

Every public top-level `def` in `app/middleware/*.sl` is a middleware named
after the **function** (not the file). `_name` functions are helpers.
Directive comments directly above the `def` configure it:

```soli
# app/middleware/auth.sl  (as generated by soli new)

# order: 20
# scope_only: true

def authenticate(req)
  api_key = req["headers"]["x-api-key"]
  if api_key.blank?
    return render_json({"error": "Unauthorized", "message": "Authentication required"}, 401)
  end

  req
end
```

```soli
# config/routes.sl
middleware("authenticate", -> {
  get("/admin", "home#admin")
})
```

Verified: `/admin` without the header → 401 JSON; with `x-api-key: k` → 200;
routes outside the block are untouched; `soli routes` lists the middleware
next to the route.

| Directive | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `# order: N` | lower runs first (default 100); scoped and global sorted together |
| `# scope_only: true` | runs only inside `middleware("name", -> { … })` |
| `# global_only: true` | runs on every request; cannot be scoped |

Return values: `req` (possibly with new keys, e.g. `req["current_user"] = …`)
continues; `render_json(...)`, `render_text(...)`, `redirect(...)` or any hash
with `"status"` stops with that response; `halt(status, msg)` raises and stops
from anywhere. There is no `# paths:`/`# methods:` directive — check
`req["path"]`/`req["method"]` in the body. Test middleware through E2E specs.

## Sessions

```soli
Session.set("user_id", 42)
Session.get("user_id")         # 42, nil when absent
Session.has("user_id")         # true
Session.delete("user_id")
Session.regenerate             # after login
Session.destroy                # logout
Session.driver                 # "in_memory" by default
```

`session_set`, `session_get`, `session_has`, `session_delete`,
`session_regenerate`, `session_destroy`, `session_id`, `session_driver`,
`session_configure` and `session_config` still run and each warns once per
process. `csrf_token()` stays a function.

Verified across requests with a cookie jar: the session cookie is
`session_id=…; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=86400`; after
`Session.destroy` the value is gone. The default `in_memory` driver is lost
on restart and not shared between processes — configure `cookie` (needs
`SOLI_SESSION_SECRET`, 32+ chars), `disk`, `solidb` or `solikv` for real use
(`SOLI_SESSION_DRIVER`; drivers other than in_memory not verified here).

After 2.39.0 (checked with the `disk` driver and in unit tests):
`Session.destroy` installs an empty session and the response sets the cookie
to its new id, so a `Session.flash` after it is kept (before: no Set-Cookie, writes
lost). A write racing a logout no longer brings the session back (0/20, was
4/20). `SOLI_SESSION_TTL` is refreshed by reads too (once a quarter of it has
passed), `SOLI_SESSION_MAX_LIFETIME` (default 30 days) caps every driver, not
only `cookie`. Disk files are `0600` in a `0700` dir and expired ones are swept
from session creation. With two cookies of one name, the **first** wins (as
Rack). An `https://` `APP_BASE_URL` makes cookies `Secure`
(`SOLI_FORCE_SECURE_COOKIES=0` opts out).

## Cookies

```soli
cookies["theme"]               # request cookies (global hash); cookies.theme also works
Cookie.set("theme", "dark", {"max_age": 3600, "http_only": true})
# → Set-Cookie: theme=dark; Path=/; Max-Age=3600; HttpOnly
Cookie.read("name")            # raw, nil when absent
```

`set_cookie` and `read_cookie` still run and each warns once per process.
The `cookies` hash is the parsed request header; it is not deprecated.

Sealed cookies (need `SOLI_SESSION_SECRET`, or `Session.configure({"secret": …})`):
`Cookie.signed("uid", 42)` writes, `Cookie.signed("uid")` reads.
`Cookie.encrypted` is the same with one argument to read and two or three to
write. The flag is forced on. A missing name reads as nil before a secret is
required. Trap: `Cookie.signed("uid", {"max_age": 60})` (a read written the
old `read_cookie(name, opts)` way) raises instead of overwriting the cookie;
store an options-shaped hash with a third argument: `Cookie.signed(n, h, {})`.
Use `Cookie.signed` / `Cookie.encrypted`, not `cookies[...]`, for a
value you must trust. `set_cookie("uid", 42, {"signed": true})` still works
and warns once.

## Flash

Flash is `Session`'s mailbox.

```soli
Session.flash("notice", "Saved!")
redirect("/next")
# next request:
Session.flashes                # [{"message": "Saved!", "type": "notice"}]; then [] after
```

`flash`, `flash_now` and `flashes` still run and each warns once per process.

## CSRF

- Apps generated by `soli new` set `SOLI_CSRF_TOKENS=require` in `.env`: a
  browser form POST without a valid `_csrf_token` gets **403** (verified).
- `form_with`, `button_to` and `csrf_field()` embed the token (plus a
  honeypot and signed timestamp used by `spam_check`). Layouts:
  `csrf_meta_tag()` for fetch/htmx (`X-CSRF-Token`).
- JSON requests are not token-gated (verified: `POST` with
  `Content-Type: application/json` succeeds). The Origin/Referer check still
  applies to browser requests; behind a proxy set `SOLI_APP_HOSTS`.
- `cors("/api/*", {"origins": ["https://app.example.com"]})` in routes for
  cross-origin APIs (documented). `skip_csrf("/path")` for webhooks (documented).

## Mass assignment — permit

```soli
permit(params, {"title": true, "body": true})              # scalars
permit(data, {"meta": {"tag": true}})                      # nested hash: only listed keys survive
permit(params, {"tags": []})                               # array of scalars (documented)
permit(params, {"days": [{"hour": true}]})                 # array of hashes (documented)
```

Verified: unlisted top-level keys and unlisted nested keys are dropped.
`soli lint` flags `Model.create(params)` in controllers/services
(`security/unfiltered-mass-assignment`).

## Passkeys

Native `WebAuthn` class (stdlib-builtins.md) + `soli generate auth --passkeys`
(cli.md). The generated sign-in mirrors the password login (per-IP throttle,
locked/confirmed/`sso_only` gates, `Session.regenerate`, `user_id` +
`session_version` + `auth_time`)
and answers every failure with the same 401, including an assertion whose
user handle is missing or names another account. The challenge lives in one
session slot (`webauthn_challenge`, purpose-tagged, 300 s TTL) and is deleted
before verification. The fetch() calls send `X-CSRF-Token` from the views'
`data-csrf-token` (the default layout has no `csrf_meta_tag()`); a
cookie-bearing JSON POST with neither Origin nor Referer is refused by the
CSRF gate, as for any other request.

## Other security behaviours (verified)

- `redirect("https://example.com")` raises (500) — local paths only.
- `halt(403, "…")` → 403 text/plain.
- Uncaught `DomainError` subclass → 422.
- `HTTP.*` refuses loopback/private hosts (SSRF guard); allow a sidecar with
  `SOLI_HTTP_ALLOW_HOSTS=127.0.0.1:9090` in the environment and request that
  literal host.
- Under `soli serve`, file builtins are jailed to the app directory.
- `password_hash`/`password_verify` are Argon2id.
